text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin –  23 To ask the Minister for Home Affairs (a) why does Singapore support the criminalisation of suicide and oppose its decriminalisation; (b) what is the psychological support provided after the Police arrests a person for attempting suicide, especially those who appear mentally unstable; (c) whether the cuffing of suicide attempters is beneficial to the psychological state of suicide attempters; and (d) what is the rehabilitation framework of admission, deterrence, treatment and aftercare phases available for those charged with and imprisoned for attempted suicide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police officers try to respond to cases of attempted suicide with sensitivity and compassion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Persons who attempt suicide are emotionally and psychologically distressed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When responding to such cases, the priority of the Police is to ensure the person's safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police Officers try to look out for signs of suicidal tendencies and take this into consideration in their response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As regards arrests, Police arrest persons for cases of attempted suicide, usually to prevent them from doing harm, either to themselves or to others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When it is assessed that there is no such risk, they may not be arrested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For all cases of attempted suicide, the Police will recommend the appropriate follow-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police may refer the person to the Samaritans of Singapore for counselling or engage the next-of-kin to assist in supporting and caring for the person.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If there are clear signs indicating possible mental instability, the Police may refer the person to the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) for an assessment of the person's mental state.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If deemed necessary by medical professionals, the person may subsequently be warded at IMH for care and treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Prison inmates who are observed to exhibit suicidal tendencies will be referred to a psychiatrist for assessment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A multidisciplinary approach is adopted and psychologists or counsellors may be involved in the management and care of the inmate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Government agencies, such as the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Ministry of Health (MOH), work closely with partners in the social services sector on programmes for public education, suicide prevention and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We should not hesitate to refer those who need support to the services that are available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I check whether this policy is cast in stone or whether the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) will consider reviewing it with the view of decriminalising attempted suicide?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to make sure that we do not inadvertently send the signal that we no longer believe that it is wrong to take one's own life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also do not want a situation where law enforcement agencies and emergency services which respond to a crisis situation where a person is attempting to take his life, in that very delicate situation, you want to make sure that those emergency services have the power and the ability to respond and to intervene.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And subsequently, to have the appropriate powers to provide support to make the necessary referrals of the individual to the various help and medical services available.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can I check if MHA provides specialist training for its officers when it comes to managing such offenders at the point of arrest, and at subsequent investigations?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I was lost as I was walking —

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: I just wanted to check with the Senior Minister of State whether MHA provides its officers with specialist training to manage such offenders at the point of arrest and at subsequent investigations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are given training, as part of their basic training, to look out for signs of suicidal tendencies, as well as the "do's" and "don'ts" in dealing with persons with such tendencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we recognise that when officers respond to the scene, they do not have full information of what is going on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We train them to be able to assess that this is a case of attempted suicide and to be able to handle this delicately.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the response to suicide risks and suicide attempts is, from the Government's perspective, one that involves a multi-prong strategy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Suicide prevention and early detection and intervention by the family,  community and by health agencies, whether Government, voluntary welfare organisations or non-government organisations, are critical.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Different Ministries, such as MSF, the Ministry of Education and MOH, work closely with stakeholders in the social services sector on suicide prevention initiatives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These programmes try to build greater resilience in the population, develop targeted intervention for high-risk individuals, and increase public awareness on mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The social services sector has an important role to play.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A couple of months ago, a couple of officers and I visited the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS).

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
